checked_scope: The finite transport identified set and the Cournot-to-monopoly example.
checks: Transport-table margins must retain the full observed within-regime pair (Cₐ,Pₐ); any feasible pair table combined with independent approval of the stated propensity attains its potential-outcome pushforward.
For the two-point margins the table has diagonals t and off-diagonals 1/2−t, 0≤t≤1/2. Strict simultaneous benefit has probability 1/2−t even though both average effects vanish.

Cournot prices give P₀=(a+2c)/3 and monopoly price P₁=(a+c−e)/2, hence benefit P₀−P₁=[3e−(a−c)]/6. Fixed-resource savings enter total efficiency but not the marginal pricing derivative; the zero-price-effect boundary is e=(a−c)/3.
limitations: Approval applies only to the review’s expressly stated mathematical scope under the manuscript assumptions. It is not human peer review, formal verification, certification of historical novelty, experimental validation, or editorial acceptance. Bibliographic third-party claims and excluded extensions were not independently certified.
